Team —

Attached is a draft priority matrix for the coming quarter and a companion role-responsibilities rubric (priority-matrix-v2.xlsx, role-rubric-v1.docx). Goal: produce a one-slide leadership readout for the QBR that clarifies where we are focusing engineering and product effort, who owns the OKRs, and what success looks like.

Three asks:
1) Quick read of the matrix and the role rubric for factual gaps (owners, timelines)
2) Call out any wording that will cause anxiety in squads — we want clarity, not surprise
3) Send redlines or a short comment thread by EOD Monday (2026-11-30) so I can lock the deck for rehearsal Tuesday.

Key decisions I want to make this week: pin the top 3 strategic priorities, finalize the p50/p95 latency targets we present externally, and name a single rollout owner per priority.

Attachments: priority-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix + swimlanes), role-rubric-v1.docx (responsibility table)

Thanks Rachel — I read the matrix. A few quick suggestions:

- Combine Priority 2 and 3 into a single priority called "Throughput & Cost Efficiency" — they overlap in owner and tradeoffs.
- For latency targets, lead with p50 as the customer-facing metric but include p95 in the appendix. Presenting both avoids overpromising.
- Add an explicit fallback owner for the rollout (e.g., EngOps lead) in case the primary is pulled into incident work.

Small wording nit: in the role rubric, the phrase "reassign squads as needed" might read as permissive reorg language to ICs. Suggest: "coordinate cross-squad priorities with Product/Eng Leads".
